To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of technology in the classroom is a complex process that requires a variety of factors to be in place.
teachers' beliefs are an important factor to consider when attempting to explain why some teachers are more successful than others at using technology in the classroom.
teacher beliefs about the role of technology in teaching and learning are related to the way they use technology to support instruction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of teachers' pedagogial beliefs and their impact on classroom practice, particularly in relation to the integration of technology in teaching and learning.
understanding and changing teachers' beliefs about the role technology should play in the classroom.
understanding the nature and impact of teacher beliefs on technology integration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
teacher beliefs about the role of technology in the classroom are a key determinant of technology use in the classroom.
teacher beliefs are important, that they influence classroom practice and that they are likely to influence the use of technology.

teachers' beliefs and attitudes are a major influence in the use of technology in the classroom and that these beliefs are not only influenced by their training, but are also influenced by their experiences with technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most significant barrier to technology integration is not a lack of access to technology, but the lack of a pedagogically sound approach to its use.
the final frontier in our efforts to integrate technology into the classroom may be in the realm of teacher pedagogical beliefs.
the conditions are in place, and that teachers are ready, but that we still do not have the whole picture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
technology is not a panacea for the challenges facing our educational system and that teachers' pedagogial beliefs are a vital component of the technology integration puzzle.
technology integration is a process, and that the process is not linear.
technology integration is not just a technical issue; it is also an issue of teacher pedagogical beliefs.
